chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: Dizzy Gillespie the man, and his book
summary: They agree Dizzy is funny and warm-hearted and helps young musicians. Dance thought his book a little controversial; Humes was given a copy but has not read it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How about that. Well, Dizzy is a funny man. He is a comical man, isn't he?
I mean, he's a very funny man.
Yeah, he's got a good heart, hasn't he?
And another thing that was nice about Dizzy is, he does alot to help musicians, bring kids along. He like to inspire people.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
He wrote a funny book though.
Did he give it to you?
Yeah. I haven't read it yet.

Well, I don't know, it was a little controversial I think. And sometimes with him doing a book like that it isn't always exactly how you would do it. Sometimes it's the way the guy that's doing it with you.

I think it was a little too much, you know, 'I am this, and this is how it was'. You know, that's a matter of opinion. I mean, when you see it written you don't get the humor with it, that would make some of the things acceptable.
